classification.difficultyReason: Requires substituting a labelled point into the circle equation, choosing the positive coordinate from the diagram, deriving the upper intercept and calculating side lengths. The preceding parts scaffold the equilateral classification, with symmetry supplying the remaining equal side.

content.prompt: In the diagram to the right, $\triangle ABC$ is inscribed in the circle $x^2+y^2=12$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 9, shared diagram to the right of parts a–d

Ordinary source blue strokes, grey axes and red point markers use house black. The Cartesian-origin O label is omitted under the graph convention.
spec.mathematics: Circle x²+y²=12; A is its positive y-intercept. B=(a,-√3) is in the fourth quadrant and C=(-a,-√3) is in the third quadrant. Coordinates used to construct the figure are not printed as answers.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source labels and givens are visible; no value of a or side length is supplied.

answer.worked:
Since $B(a,-\sqrt3)$ lies on the circle,
$$\begin{align*}a^2+(-\sqrt3)^2&=12\\a^2+3&=12\\a^2&=9\\a&=3\end{align*}$$
The diagram places $B$ to the right of the $y$-axis, so $a$ is positive.

At the upper $y$-intercept, $x=0$ and $y>0$, so $A=(0,\sqrt{12})=(0,2\sqrt3)$. Also, $B=(3,-\sqrt3)$.
$$\begin{align*}AB^2&=(3-0)^2+(-\sqrt3-2\sqrt3)^2\\AB^2&=9+(-3\sqrt3)^2\\AB^2&=9+27\\AB^2&=36\\AB&=6\end{align*}$$
